sourceNote: Catalog has two sources: (1) https://anthropic.skilljar.com/ — Anthropic's live LMS, 18 courses, the live video versions; (2) https://github.com/anthropics/courses — Anthropic's open-source CC BY-NC 4.0 course notebooks, 5 courses that historically existed as standalone Skilljar courses and are now consolidated into Building with the Claude API. Each entry's `source` field indicates which catalog it comes from. GitHub-sourced courses carry `attribution` metadata; non-commercial use only.

courses.title: Claude 101
courses.summary: Learn how to use Claude for everyday work tasks, understand core features, and explore resources for more advanced learning.
learningObjectives: Describe what Claude is and where it shows up (chat, desktop, Cowork, Code)
Have a productive first conversation and refine prompts that don't land
Use projects to keep context across many conversations
Build with artifacts, work with skills, and connect Claude to your tools
Recognize when to use Research mode and enterprise search
Know what Claude is good at — and where to be careful

courses.title: Anthropic API fundamentals
courses.summary: Essentials of working with the Claude SDK: getting an API key, working with model parameters, writing multimodal prompts, streaming responses.
learningObjectives: Set up and authenticate with the Claude SDK
Send messages and tune model parameters
Stream responses
Build multimodal prompts (text + images)

attribution.creator: Anthropic

courses.title: Prompt Engineering Interactive Tutorial
courses.summary: Comprehensive step-by-step guide to key prompting techniques: structure, clarity, roles, separating data from instructions, output formatting, chain-of-thought, examples, avoiding hallucinations, and building complex prompts. Plus an appendix on chaining, tool use, and retrieval.
learningObjectives: Master the basic structure of a good prompt
Recognize common failure modes and the '80/20' techniques to address them
Understand Claude's strengths and weaknesses
Build strong prompts from scratch for real use cases

attribution.creator: Anthropic
attribution.notes: Adapted from Anthropic's open-source Prompt Engineering Interactive Tutorial. Non-commercial use only.

courses.title: Real World Prompting
courses.summary: Take the prompting techniques from the Interactive Tutorial and apply them to messy, real production prompts.
learningObjectives: Design prompts that survive messy real input
Ground answers in source material
Iterate prompts using small evaluation sets
Decide when to use a system prompt vs. user content

attribution.creator: Anthropic

courses.title: Prompt Evaluations
courses.summary: Build evaluation sets to measure prompt quality and catch regressions.
learningObjectives: Construct a small but useful eval set
Choose between exact-match, model-graded, and human grading
Track regressions across prompt iterations
Wire evals into a deployment workflow

courses.title: Tool Use

learningObjectives: Define a tool schema Claude understands
Handle the request → tool_use → tool_result loop
